newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ mid-bonds rally at close after talk of samurai.
newsitem.headline: NZ mid-bonds rally at close after talk of samurai.

text.p: FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD
OVERNIGHT CASH 10.05 PCT (UNCH) US 30-YR 6.93
* NZ 3-yr bonds rally at close after samurai rumour
* Bank bill futures bounce back from lows
New Zealand mid bonds rallied around five basis points at Tuesday's close on talk of samurai pricing, after looking "a bit dodgy" earlier in the day.
Dealers said they had heard rumours of NZ$400-450 million worth of samurai going through, but had seen no evidence of it themselves.
"Either the flow gets fed or the rumour dissipates, so we might get back into the same frame that we had this morning," one money market dealer said.
A bond dealer was more optimistic.
"After such a good day today, it should probably continue to trek a bit lower, I should imagine," he said.

The 7/98s shed six points to close at eight percent, while the 02/00s lost five to 8.06 percent. Longer bonds finished around last night's closing levels, with the 11/06s still a couple of points away from the crucial eight percent mark.
Money market dealers said flows were light in the physicals but quite reasonable in the futures, with 1,622 of the front contracts traded and good buying interest seen from Australia.
The December contracts traded as low as 90.53 for about five contracts, and spent a bit of time at 90.54 before bouncing back after lunch to close at 90.60.
A T-bill tender just after lunch attracted good bidding interest at reasonable levels, dealers said.

A bill dealer said now that the FOMC in the U.S. had been and gone, the market was focusing on New Zealand's general election on October 12, and any offshore investment seen in samurais and eurokiwis.
"With the market having little else to concentrate on, there seems to be persistent selling interest. Nothing big, but it's there," he said.
"But at the same time, as soon as talk of the samurai issue comes through all that offering has gone," he added.

New Zealand mid bonds outperformed both the U.S. and Australia in a solid day's trade on the back of rumours of a samurai. Dealers put the strong showing down purely to recent offshore investment in New Zealand. "They're chasing the yields," one said.
